children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares slipped on Thursday despite stellar September trade data, as elevated global oil prices and uncertainty over the sustainability of recovering Middle East oil flows clouded risk sentiment.
** The won weakened, while the benchmark bond yield rose. ** The benchmark KOSPI
was down 14.60 points, or 0.21%, at 6,823.44 as of 00:56 GMT.  ** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
gained 0.23%. ** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution

** South Korea's exports jumped 83.5% in September to a record $120.9 billion year-on-year, government data showed on Thursday, as semiconductor shipments more than tripled on global spending on artificial intelligence.

** US President Donald Trump unveiled plans on Wednesday for South Korea to invest some $200 billion in US projects, but Seoul quickly suggested one key element, a $54 billion pipeline for an LNG project in Alaska, was not yet set in stone. ** Of the total 905 traded issues, 354 shares advanced, while 487 declined. ** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 494.4 billion won. ** The won was quoted at 1,359.4 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform

, 0.27% lower than its previous close at 1,355.7. ** The KOSPI has risen 61.92% so far this year. ** The won has strengthened 5.9% against the dollar so far this year. ** In money and debt markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.07 point to 102.30. ** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose 2.4 basis points to 4.035%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
